details:
I would like a new moderation reporting category for misleading world thumbnails. It is becoming an increasing problem of AI “enhanced” thumbnails where authors are taking a screenshot of a world and then running it through and AI and asking it to “enhance” it or “make it look photorealistic”. It is becoming an increasing problem for exploration/ world-hopping where you now have to carefully inspect each thumbnail before clicking in order to check you aren’t being bamboozled. To be clear I don’t care about thumbnails where the entire thing is an AI generated logo or graphic, they’re ugly but not misleading. This reporting category is not just for AI either, it would also cover worlds where the author uploads an unrelated photo, or takes a photo of a plane in the world. 

Things this report category would cover:

- AI enhanced/generated screenshots

- Unrelated/stock photos of a place/location

- Thirst-trap images

- Screenshot of a plane in the world if it fits into one of the above categories.

Things this reporting category would NOT cover:

- Screenshots of an older version of the world.

- Meme images / other images that do not look like a place/location 

- Plain logos, regardless of AI-generation.

The key is that this would be to prevent **Misleading** thumbnails, anything that entices a visit that isn’t actually representative of the world. Especially in a way that is outright lying to get clicks, as is becoming so common lately.
title: New report category: Misleading Thumbnail
